name: 123 Manitou
headline: A 50-home, all income-restricted new family rental community on the former La Fon (La Fun) Motel site at 123 Manitou Avenue, co-sponsored by Paragon Development and TWG Development, won 2026 Round One federal 9% and state housing tax credits from CHFA.
why_it_matters: It is the first Housing Tax Credit apartment property in Manitou Springs, and it won on a second try after the sponsors added units, a county housing trust fund commitment, conditional state Division of Housing money and a housing authority partnership for tax exemption.

status.label: Credits awarded; city approvals and construction start not confirmed
status.detail: CHFA reserved the credits in Round One (announced 2026-05-21). As of mid-June 2026 the project still needed Planning Commission, Pikes Peak Regional Building Department and City Council approval; the sponsors and the urban renewal authority expect construction to start in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027, with residents by 2028. No permit, closing or groundbreaking record was found.

next_step: Watch Manitou Springs Planning Commission and City Council agendas for the final building plan hearing, then the Pikes Peak Regional Building permit and the financing closing.

background.text: The site held the historic La Fon Motel (briefly the La Fun Motel); Paragon bought it in 2022 with a $2.1 million urban renewal authority investment and demolished the motel, which officials had called a public safety hazard.
The application says the city helped with demolition, removal of the prior problematic ownership and site cleanup, completed in 2023.
Paragon first proposed 78 market-rate units in two buildings; the site's zoning caps density at 20 units per acre, and in December 2024 the Planning Commission voted 4-3 to deny the density variance.
Paragon then teamed with TWG on a 43-unit tax credit plan; City Council unanimously approved a letter of support at a 28 January 2025 special meeting (year inferred from the article date).
The 2025 Round One application (43 units, 9 at 30%, 3 at 40%, 9 at 50%, 22 at 60% AMI) did not win; it is not on CHFA's 2025 Round One award report.

For 2026 the sponsors raised density to 50 units, obtained conditional Division of Housing funding and an El Paso County Housing Trust Fund commitment, raised the energy standard and added Rainbow Housing services.
El Paso County Housing Authority is to join the partnership as special limited partner to provide property tax and sales and use tax exemption.
Manitou Springs committed under Prop 123 to permit 46 new affordable units; this project alone would meet that commitment, according to the application.
Local officials in June 2026 cited city funds, developer money and a state Prop 123 grant toward the project, without amounts; a one-bedroom example rent of about $650 a month was given.
TWG's own later CHFA application (Castleton Heights, 2026 Round Two) says it expects to deliver the 50 units at 123 Manitou in 2028.

discrepancies.text: The site size differs: The Gazette calls it a 2-acre property and the Pikes Peak Bulletin a 2.2-acre lot, while Rocky Mountain PBS says 56,000 square feet (about 1.3 acres).
The urban renewal authority's press release puts Round One federal awards at $23,003,741 for 14 developments, while CHFA's award report totals $23,509,805 in federal 9% credit.
The Pikes Peak Bulletin described TWG Development as Colorado-based, while The Gazette describes it as Indiana-based.
